RagShortTexts: The Olgovichi retreated into Bryansk forest keeps after Mongol devastation, preserving.

Variants.Content: The Olgovichi traced their descent from Oleg of Chernigov and held a princely title older than many Rus principalities. Their lands around Chernigov and the Bryansk forests lay along the upper Desna, a belt of marsh, pine and clearing that made large steppe armies slow and easy to ambush. The princes kept a druzhina, a professional core of mounted retainers, and built stone churches whose painted walls sealed their claim to the Orthodox patrimony. Michael of Chernigov's death at the Horde in 1246 became the family's sacred memory, kept alive through the saints' lives that praised his refusal to bow before idols. Tribute to the Golden Horde was paid in furs, silver and levies, but the forests let the princes delay collection.

A boyar prince of Chernigov weighed every treaty against the steppe. Gifts of furs and silver went to Horde officials to keep the tax roll light, while agents watched Lithuanian envoys in Bryansk for signs of an incoming raid. Marriage alliances with neighbouring Rurikid houses kept any single rival's betrayal from isolating the forest keeps.
